newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan April M2 money supply up 9.76 percent.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan April M2 money supply up 9.76 percent.

text.p: Taiwan's broadest money supply measure, M2, grew 9.76 percent in April from a year earlier, the central bank said on Saturday.

April was the fourth straight month in which the central bank used a revised definition of M2 measure. Analysts have said the new broader definition could be expected to add 1.0 to 1.5 percentage points to the figure.
The year-on-year April M2 increase was lower than an average forecast of 10.12 percent complied from a May 22 Reuters poll of Taiwan economists.
M2 grew a year-on-year 9.90 percent in March.
The central bank attributed the low April M2 money supply growth to reducing foreign assets of financial institutions.
Economists have noted that demand for money was slowly increasing due to a recovering domestic economy.
"Money demand has kept on rising due to the domestic recovery, and the central bank apparently has not tightened liquidity," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.
Until January, the central bank's money supply categories were defined as follows:
--M1A: cash, checking accounts and passbook deposits

In in the revision, the bank said it would maintain its M1A and M1B definition unchanged, while M2 now would include M1B plus time deposits, foreign currency deposits, postal funds, repurchase agreement trade outstanding and foreigners' Taiwan dollar holdings.

The new M2 definition uses post offices' total deposits instead of their redeposits in banks, adds repurchase agreement trade outstanding and foreigners' Taiwan dollar holdings, and deletes the net value of financial bonds, savings bonds and treasury bills and foreign-currency trust funds.
